d: The International University of Science & Technology in Kuwait (IUK) is a newly established private university in Kuwait, with a new Campus located in the heart of Kuwait near the Avenues Mall. Fully accredited by the Private Universities Council (PUC), the University offers a wide range of academic programs in three Colleges; namely: College of Engineering, College of Business Administration, and College of Arts. In addition to the academic programs, the IUK has established the University Foundation Program (UFP) that offers English and Math foundation programs. The IUK is looking for dynamic full-time faculty members who are passionate about teaching, and contributing to the development of a vibrant and successful learning environment for students.

The College of Engineering invites applications for positions at the level of Assistant/Associate Professor in Computer Science & Cyber Security. In addition to Computer Science & Cyber Security, the College offers several Bachelor’s programs in Engineering (Computer, Electrical, Industrial, Civil & Architectural, Architecture & Design and Biomedical Engineering).

The primary role of the faculty members is to promote high-quality teaching, research and creative work, university services, and to mentor junior colleagues. Besides, the candidate will collaborate with the Head of Department, Dean, and colleagues to achieve the Department’s and College’s mission and vision, in line with the IUK’s vision, and support the department with academic and administrative services.

Reporting to the Department Chair, the successful candidate will be responsible for the development, delivery, and evaluation of a broad range of courses within Computer Science and Cyber Security such as ethical hacking and Industrial Control Systems (ICS) Security, to name a few. In addition to teaching, successful candidates are expected to maintain significant scholarly work and professional services. The successful candidate will contribute to developing an outcome-based student-focused curriculum. In addition, faculty members are expected to maintain office hours, provide advisement for students, participate in curriculum development, and contribute to the university’s professional development activities.
q: A Ph.D. in a computing field with a dissertation (or intensive research/teaching) in Cyber Security.
A minimum of three years of university teaching experience for assistant professor and five years for associate professor at a university level.

A proven research record, scholarly work, publications, and knowledge transfer. A minimum of three journal articles in peer-reviewed indexed journals (ISI or Scopus) for assistant professor and five years for associate professor.
Proven experience in using different learning management systems and in adopting e-learning teaching strategies.
Experience that proves an understanding of a multicultural academic environment, and understanding of students’ needs, including those of special needs.
Commitment to excellence in teaching and scholarship.
Experience in course design based on the OBE model is an asset.

d: Our client: A renowned group of companies with diverse business interests and international investments. The group's interests span multiple businesses, ownership structures and jurisdictions, creating a legal environment where commercial transactions, corporate governance, shareholder interests and day-to-day operating decisions frequently intersect.

Your role: This is a seat at the table where business ambition, shareholder interests and legal risk meet. You will work closely with shareholders and the board, helping them navigate major investments, complex transactions, disputes and ownership matters. Your value lies in making the difficult calls: when to push a deal forward, when to change its structure and when to advise against it.

You will need to understand the interests behind the instructions, reconcile competing priorities and hold your ground when the business needs clear advice. Trust, discretion and the ability to handle sensitive shareholder conversations will matter as much as technical legal depth.
r: Shareholder and board counsel: Advise on ownership structures, shareholder rights, governance and private investment matters. Bring clarity to sensitive decisions and secure alignment on how to proceed.

Transactions and capital: Lead the legal work on acquisitions, investments, joint ventures and financing. Shape the terms early, negotiate the protections that matter and carry transactions through to completion.

Commercial exposure: Understand where risk sits across businesses and jurisdictions. Address weak contractual positions, unclear obligations and unresolved liabilities before they become expensive problems.

Disputes and negotiations: Set the strategy for litigation, arbitration and settlements. Make clear recommendations on what to defend, negotiate or resolve, with commercial consequences firmly in view.
Legal leadership: Build a responsive legal function, develop the internal team and hold external advisers accountable for the quality, cost and usefulness of their advice.

Shareholders and the board involve you before commitments are made. Transactions move with clear terms and understood risks. Major disputes have a deliberate strategy, realistic cost exposure and a route to resolution. Governance works in practice, and the legal team earns the confidence of business leaders through the quality of its judgement and execution.

Must-haves: A professionally qualified lawyer with substantial senior legal experience. You should have helmed the legal function for diverse business entities. You will bring GCC experience, meaningful European exposure and a record of advising shareholders and boards directly.
Arabic and English capability is strongly preferred.
